audit.why: Emerald+ 51.89% over 2139 games, matches the table.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nowhere does the entry mention that Decisive Strike breaks slows.
audit.why: Kit text: "Garen gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him." Tahm Kench's Tongue Lash slow is his only tool for holding a melee champion in range, and Garen deletes it on an 8-second, no-cost button. The entry talks at length about the silence but never tells the player that the slow half of Q is equally negated — which is why the "slow him out of CS" plan in content.early stops working the moment Garen hits 2.
audit.corrected: The slow-break now stated in spikes[0], whys[1], early and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull make Courage the matchup-defining cooldown.
audit.why: Courage is a 22s damage-reduction button; Decisive Strike is an 8-second, free ability that both silences Devour away and cancels your slow. The thing you must count is the 8s, not the 22s — tracking the wrong cooldown is what makes a player commit into a live silence.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns re-pointed to Decisive Strike with its 8s figure. Courage remains correctly described elsewhere (its tenacity clipping your stun duration is already right in wants.you[2] and whys[2]).

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early says "you must reach 3 stacks BEFORE you open your W" and "never W first into a Garen who still has his Q available".
audit.why: W is Abyssal Dive. The ability being silenced away is Devour (R). Another pre-rework slot leftover, and here it actively misdirects — it tells the player to protect the wrong button.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around Devour and the real sequencing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly sells a "Q-stun then Devour" chain as one combo.
audit.why: Riot's own text in the kit: An Acquired Taste — "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion"; Tongue Lash — "If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." The stun and the swallow draw on the same three stacks, so a Q cast at 3 stacks stuns and destroys the resource Devour requires. The real sequence is to let Q land the THIRD stack (which does not stun) and then press R.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as: build to three, let Q apply the third stack, Devour immediately; a Q thrown at an enemy already on 3 stacks stuns but burns the swallow.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry credits Tahm Kench with "Abyssal Voyage" 2 time(s) and treats it as a global/roaming ultimate.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage was removed in the Tahm Kench rework. The kit file lists W = Abyssal Dive and R = Devour; there is no global travel ability in the kit at all. Advice built on "use Abyssal Voyage to roam / reposition cross-map" tells the player to press a button that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Every reference re-pointed to Devour (R) or Abyssal Dive (W) as appropriate, with the surrounding advice rewritten so it describes what those abilities actually do.

audit.why: Demacian Justice is correctly identified as a true-damage execute (it is the one R in this slice the kit does flag `execute`), and spikes[3] correctly warns against idling at low HP. No change.

edits.before: Garen's Q comes online — the silence interrupts your Devour mid-cast, so every punish attempt before 3 stacks risks a silenced W and a free Judgment spin on you.
edits.after: Decisive Strike comes online — its silence denies Devour and it breaks your Tongue Lash slow on cast, so any punish before 3 stacks risks a free Judgment.

edits.before: At level 1, Tongue Lash's range lets you slow Garen out of CS and begin stacking An Acquired Taste from a distance he cannot match — he has no ranged tool to retaliate. The catch is that once he hits level 2 and presses Q, that silence flat cancels a Devour cast mid-animation, so you must reach 3 stacks BEFORE you open your W or the whole combo falls apart. Trade pattern: Tongue Lash, auto, Tongue Lash again to reach 3 stacks from range, THEN Devour — never W first into a Garen who still has his Q available. His passive regen means he recovers between your skirmishes, so be prepared to fish for the stun repeatedly rather than winning a single all-in.
edits.after: At level 1, Tongue Lash's range lets you slow Garen out of CS and begin stacking An Acquired Taste from a distance he cannot match — he has no ranged tool to retaliate. The catch is that once he presses Decisive Strike the silence denies Devour outright, and the same cast breaks your Tongue Lash slow, so he leaves whenever he likes. Trade pattern: Tongue Lash, auto, Tongue Lash for the third stack, THEN Devour — a Q thrown at 3 stacks stuns and burns what Devour needs. His passive regen means he recovers between your skirmishes, so be prepared to fish for the stun repeatedly rather than winning a single all-in.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a patient chess game — Garen wants to Q in, spin, and back off before you stack him, and his Courage tenacity cuts the duration of your empowered Q stun when you finally land it. Play the wave to force him to walk up, stack Tongue Lash on his approach, and time the all-in for after his Q silence is on cooldown so your Devour connects cleanly. At level 6 his Demacian Justice becomes the dominant threat in the lane: if you sit on low HP fishing for grey-health recovery and he Rs, you die. Convert your Thick Skin grey-health into the shield proactively when you dip below 40% rather than waiting — and use Abyssal Voyage to roam when the lane stalls rather than taking bad short trades into a Courage-stacked Garen.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a patient chess game — Garen wants Decisive Strike in, Judgment, and out before you stack him, and his Courage tenacity cuts the duration of your empowered Q stun when you finally land it. Play the wave to force him to walk up, stack Tongue Lash on his approach, and time the all-in for after his Q silence is on cooldown so your Devour connects cleanly. At level 6 his Demacian Justice becomes the dominant threat in the lane: if you sit on low HP fishing for grey-health recovery and he Rs, you die. Convert your Thick Skin grey-health into the shield proactively when you dip below 40% rather than waiting — and hold Devour for his Demacian Justice window rather than taking bad short trades into a Courage-stacked Garen.

edits.before: Garen's Q silence at level 2 cancels Devour mid-cast — he controls the trade pattern the moment that ability is up and you have not yet reached 3 stacks.
edits.after: Decisive Strike denies Devour and eats your slow, all on 8s — he controls the trade pattern the moment that ability is up and you have not yet reached 3 stacks.

edits.before: Abyssal Voyage adds global threat but his Demacian Justice execute means sitting on grey-health near death is dangerous — you cannot be passive about the Thick Skin shield conversion.
edits.after: Devour arrives, but Demacian Justice executes on missing health, so sitting on grey-health near death is dangerous — you cannot be passive about the Thick Skin shield conversion.

edits.before: Q-silence you at the start of every trade to cancel Devour and strip your lockdown before you reach 3 stacks
edits.after: Open every trade with Decisive Strike — it silences Devour away and shrugs off your Tongue Lash slow at once

edits.before: Respect his Courage window — wait for the W tenacity to expire before landing your empowered Q stun so the full duration locks him in place
edits.after: Respect his Courage window — wait for Courage's tenacity to lapse before landing the 3-stack Q stun so the full duration locks him in place

edits.before: - Garen Courage: matchup-defining — Damage reduction. Trade when down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Garen Decisive Strike: matchup-defining — Silence + slow-break, 8s. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: Decisive Strike breaking slows was the missing piece — the entry's level-1 plan ("slow Garen out of CS") quietly expires at level 2 and nothing said so. Courage granting tenacity was already handled correctly, which is unusual and worth keeping.
